newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SSL to spend U.S.$23 mln on Saigon stake.
newsitem.headline: SSL to spend U.S.$23 mln on Saigon stake.

text.p: Property company Straits Steamship Land Ltd (SSL) said on Tuesday it would spend U.S.$23 million to take a controlling interest in the Saigon Centre office development in Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City.
SSL said in a statement it would buy the 50 percent stake held by Hong Kong-based First Pacific Land Ltd (FPL) in the centre, raising the SSL shareholding to 68 percent.

FPL was selling its stake after parent company First Pacific Davies Ltd (FPD) decided to become an integrated property services business rather than a pure developer, FPD managing director David Davies said in the SSL statement.
Davies said FPL was disposing of various real estate interests in Thailand, Hong Kong and China.
The centre's Vietnamese partners remain The Waterborne Transport Corporation No. 2 and the Housing Management Trading Company of Ho Chi Minh City, which hold a 32 percent interest.
SSL said an occupation permit had been obtaind for phase one of the 25-storey Saigon Centre. Other phases would be developed over time in line with market needs, the company said.
SSL said it had signed Deutsche Bank as a tenant to lease more than 20 percent of the office space in the phase one tower for a period of 15 years.
No financial details of the lease were disclosed.
SSL, part of Singapore conglomerate Keppel Corp, is to to be renamed Keppel Land Ltd as part of a corporate rebranding due to be completed by the end of February.
